## Exploring Conditional Average Treatment Effects

This is an side exploration of CATE based on Tennant's estimand of a follow-up measure adjusted for baseline values @tennant2021:

$$
E[Y_1^x - Y_1^{x'} | Y_0 = y_0]
$$

This is typically the effect in the substrata where $Y_0 = y_0$ , but

```{r}
library(grf)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(123)

# Generate data
n <- 2000
age <- runif(n, 18, 70)
male <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
treatment <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)

# True CATE with interaction
true_cate <- 1 + 0.05 * age + 0.5 * male + 0.02 * age * male

# Outcome
baseline <- 50 + 0.3 * age + 2 * male
y <- baseline + treatment * true_cate + rnorm(n, 0, 5)

data <- data.frame(y, treatment, male, age, true_cate)

# ============================================================
# Method 1: Linear Regression CATE
# ============================================================

# Fit regression with treatment interactions
lm_cate <- lm(y ~ treatment * (age + male), data = data)
summary(lm_cate)

# Extract CATE predictions
# CATE = coefficient on treatment + interaction coefficients × covariate values
data$cate_lm <- predict(lm_cate, 
                        newdata = data %>% mutate(treatment = 1)) -
                predict(lm_cate, 
                        newdata = data %>% mutate(treatment = 0))

# ============================================================
# Method 2: Causal Forest CATE (for comparison)
# ============================================================

X <- data %>% select(male, age)
cf <- causal_forest(X, data$y, data$treatment, num.trees = 2000)
data$cate_cf <- predict(cf)$predictions

# ============================================================
# Compare the methods
# ============================================================

cat("=== LINEAR REGRESSION CATE ===\n")
cat("Model coefficients:\n")
print(coef(lm_cate))
cat("\n")

# Show how to interpret coefficients for CATE
cat("CATE formula from regression:\n")
cat("CATE(age, male) = ", round(coef(lm_cate)["treatment"], 2), 
    " + ", round(coef(lm_cate)["treatment:age"], 3), " × age",
    " + ", round(coef(lm_cate)["treatment:male"], 2), " × male\n\n", sep="")

# Example predictions
cat("Example CATEs from linear regression:\n")
cat("Young female (age 20, male=0):", round(coef(lm_cate)["treatment"] + 
                                              coef(lm_cate)["treatment:age"]*20, 2), "\n")
cat("Old male (age 65, male=1):", round(coef(lm_cate)["treatment"] + 
                                          coef(lm_cate)["treatment:age"]*65 + 
                                          coef(lm_cate)["treatment:male"], 2), "\n\n")

# ============================================================
# Visualization: Compare methods
# ============================================================

# Plot 1: True vs predicted CATEs
p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = true_cate)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cate_lm, color = "Linear Regression"), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cate_cf, color = "Causal Forest"), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Linear Regression" = "blue", 
                                "Causal Forest" = "red"),
                    name = "Method") +
  labs(title = "True CATE vs Predicted CATE",
       x = "True CATE",
       y = "Predicted CATE") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p1)

# Plot 2: CATE by age for males and females
plot_data <- data.frame(
  age = rep(seq(18, 70, length.out = 100), 2),
  male = rep(c(0, 1), each = 100)
)

# Predict using linear regression
plot_data$cate_lm <- predict(lm_cate, 
                              newdata = plot_data %>% mutate(treatment = 1)) -
                     predict(lm_cate, 
                              newdata = plot_data %>% mutate(treatment = 0))

# Add true CATE
plot_data$true_cate <- 1 + 0.05 * plot_data$age + 0.5 * plot_data$male + 
                       0.02 * plot_data$age * plot_data$male

p2 <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = age, color = factor(male))) +
  geom_line(aes(y = true_cate, linetype = "True CATE"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cate_lm, linetype = "Linear Regression"), size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "purple", "1" = "blue"),
                     labels = c("Female", "Male"),
                     name = "Sex") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("True CATE" = "solid", 
                                   "Linear Regression" = "dashed"),
                        name = "Type") +
  labs(title = "CATE by Age and Sex: Linear Regression vs True",
       x = "Age",
       y = "Treatment Effect") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p2)

# ============================================================
# Performance metrics
# ============================================================

cat("=== PERFORMANCE COMPARISON ===\n")
cat("Linear Regression:\n")
cat("  RMSE:", round(sqrt(mean((data$cate_lm - data$true_cate)^2)), 3), "\n")
cat("  Correlation with true CATE:", round(cor(data$cate_lm, data$true_cate), 3), "\n\n")

cat("Causal Forest:\n")
cat("  RMSE:", round(sqrt(mean((data$cate_cf - data$true_cate)^2)), 3), "\n")
cat("  Correlation with true CATE:", round(cor(data$cate_cf, data$true_cate), 3), "\n\n")

# ============================================================
# Show when linear regression CATE fails
# ============================================================

cat("=== WHEN LINEAR REGRESSION WORKS WELL ===\n")
cat("Linear regression CATE works great when:\n")
cat("1. Treatment effects are truly linear in covariates\n")
cat("2. You know which interactions to include\n")
cat("3. The functional form is correctly specified\n\n")

# Generate data with non-linear CATE
set.seed(456)
n <- 2000
age <- runif(n, 18, 70)
treatment <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)

# Non-linear true CATE
true_cate_nonlin <- 2 + 0.5 * sin(age / 10)  # sinusoidal effect

baseline <- 50 + 0.3 * age
y_nonlin <- baseline + treatment * true_cate_nonlin + rnorm(n, 0, 5)

data_nonlin <- data.frame(y = y_nonlin, treatment, age, true_cate = true_cate_nonlin)

# Linear regression (misspecified)
lm_cate_wrong <- lm(y ~ treatment * age, data = data_nonlin)
data_nonlin$cate_lm <- predict(lm_cate_wrong, 
                                newdata = data_nonlin %>% mutate(treatment = 1)) -
                       predict(lm_cate_wrong, 
                                newdata = data_nonlin %>% mutate(treatment = 0))

# Causal forest (flexible)
cf_nonlin <- causal_forest(matrix(data_nonlin$age), 
                           data_nonlin$y, 
                           data_nonlin$treatment, 
                           num.trees = 2000)
data_nonlin$cate_cf <- predict(cf_nonlin)$predictions

# Plot non-linear case
p3 <- data_nonlin %>%
  arrange(age) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = true_cate, color = "True CATE"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = cate_lm, color = "Linear Regression"), 
              method = "loess", se = FALSE, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = cate_cf, color = "Causal Forest"), 
              method = "loess", se = FALSE, size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("True CATE" = "black",
                                "Linear Regression" = "blue",
                                "Causal Forest" = "red"),
                     name = "Method") +
  labs(title = "When Linear Regression CATE Fails: Non-linear Treatment Effects",
       subtitle = "Linear regression imposes wrong functional form",
       x = "Age",
       y = "Treatment Effect") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p3)

cat("=== NON-LINEAR CASE PERFORMANCE ===\n")
cat("Linear Regression RMSE:", 
    round(sqrt(mean((data_nonlin$cate_lm - data_nonlin$true_cate)^2)), 3), "\n")
cat("Causal Forest RMSE:", 
    round(sqrt(mean((data_nonlin$cate_cf - data_nonlin$true_cate)^2)), 3), "\n")
```
